definition: A classifier and projection method using shared-covariance class-conditional Gaussian assumptions.
example: Separate labeled groups with a linear boundary.
caveat: LDA also abbreviates latent Dirichlet allocation.

definition: A learned matrix transformation, usually with an optional additive bias.
example: Project a hidden vector into class scores.
caveat: With a bias, the mapping is affine rather than strictly linear.

definition: A linear diagnostic model fitted to fixed representations.
example: Test whether a concept is linearly decodable.
caveat: Probe accuracy alone does not establish a causal mechanism.

definition: Predicting a numeric target as a weighted sum of features, commonly fitted by squared error.
example: Estimate house prices from area and age.
caveat: Linearity is in parameters; transformed features can still be nonlinear in inputs.

definition: A collection of linear equations whose solution satisfies all equations simultaneously.
example: Solve for regression coefficients or a Newton step.
caveat: A system may have no solution, one solution, or many solutions.

definition: Predicting missing or future relationships between pairs of graph nodes.
example: Recommend likely connections in a network.
caveat: Evaluation must account for temporal leakage and negative sampling.

definition: The rule defining distance between clusters during hierarchical clustering.
example: Use complete linkage to compare farthest member pairs.
caveat: Different linkage rules can yield different hierarchies.

definition: A bound on how quickly outputs can change relative to inputs under selected norms.
example: Reason about stability and robustness.
caveat: A bound can be very loose in large networks.

definition: A ranking objective defined over a full candidate list or its ordering.
example: Optimize a document ranking list.
caveat: List construction affects the training signal.

definition: Using a language model to score, compare, or critique outputs under an evaluation rubric.
example: Triage generated answers for human review.
caveat: Agreement with a judge is not independent proof of correctness.

definition: Operational practices for language-model applications, including prompts, retrieval, evaluation, serving, and monitoring.
example: Track changes to a production RAG application.
caveat: The label does not define one standardized tool stack.

definition: An auxiliary objective encouraging balanced use of experts or computational resources.
example: Prevent a small number of experts from receiving most tokens.
caveat: Balancing can conflict with specialization.

definition: A point with no lower objective value in a sufficiently small neighborhood.
example: An optimizer settles in a local basin.
caveat: It need not be the best point overall.

definition: An outlier score comparing a point's local density with its neighbors' densities.
example: Detect locally unusual observations.
caveat: Training-data outlier detection and novelty modes differ.

definition: Hashing designed so similar items are more likely to share buckets.
example: Approximate similarity search at scale.
caveat: The hash family must fit the chosen similarity.

definition: A method preserving local linear reconstruction relationships in a low-dimensional embedding.
example: Represent a nonlinear manifold.
caveat: Neighborhood selection affects stability.

definition: Negative log probability assigned to observed labels, typically averaged over examples.
example: Penalize confidently wrong predictions.
caveat: Extreme incorrect probabilities can dominate the score.

definition: Applying a logarithm to change scale or reduce multiplicative skew.
example: Transform a positive, heavy-tailed spending feature.
caveat: Zero and negative values require deliberate handling.

definition: A distribution of positive values whose logarithms follow a normal distribution.
example: Model positive quantities with multiplicative variability.
caveat: Its mean is not simply the exponential of the underlying normal mean.

definition: The logarithm of p divided by one minus p for a binary probability.
example: Interpret a logistic-regression score.
caveat: Probabilities zero and one correspond to infinite log-odds.

definition: The logarithm of softmax computed in a numerically stable form.
example: Calculate token log probabilities.
caveat: Computing log after a naive softmax can be less stable.

definition: The logarithm of a sum of exponentials, often computed by subtracting the largest input for numerical stability.
example: Normalize log probabilities safely.
caveat: Direct exponentiation can overflow even when the final value is representable.

definition: A classification model mapping linear scores to probabilities using a logistic or softmax link.
example: Estimate the probability an email is spam.
caveat: Despite its name, it is commonly used for classification.

definition: An unnormalized model score; for a binary probability, also the log-odds transform.
example: Score each possible next token before softmax.
caveat: General multiclass logits are defined only up to a shared additive constant.

definition: Transferring knowledge by matching teacher output logits or derived distributions.
example: Minimize divergence between teacher and student predictions.
caveat: Matching raw logits and matching probabilities are different objectives.

definition: Projecting intermediate representations into output-token space to inspect provisional predictions.
example: View layer-by-layer token preferences.
caveat: Early-layer representations may not be calibrated for the final output head.

definition: A function modifying output scores before token selection.
example: Suppress invalid tokens or apply repetition penalties.
caveat: Processors can change the model's sampling distribution.

definition: Testing how a model uses information across long inputs rather than only whether it accepts them.
example: Measure reasoning over evidence spread through a large document.
caveat: A long supported window does not imply uniformly reliable use.

definition: The longest ordered sequence shared by two sequences, without requiring adjacent positions.
example: Compare text sequences in ROUGE-L-style evaluation.
caveat: A subsequence is not necessarily a contiguous substring.

definition: A scaling hyperparameter controlling the magnitude of a LoRA update under its chosen convention.
example: Scale an adapter relative to base weights.
caveat: Scaling formulas differ for standard and rank-stabilized LoRA.

definition: The dimension of the low-rank factors used in a LoRA update.
example: Choose how much capacity a LoRA adapter has.
caveat: Higher rank increases trainable size but does not guarantee better results.

definition: A function measuring how undesirable a prediction or model outcome is.
example: Penalize incorrect class probabilities.
caveat: Loss and evaluation metric need not be the same.

definition: The objective value viewed as a function of model parameters.
example: Study curvature near a trained solution.
caveat: Low-dimensional visualizations can be misleading.

definition: Excluding selected positions from the training loss.
example: Train only on assistant response tokens.
caveat: Loss masking does not prevent those positions from influencing later activations.

definition: Multiplying the loss before backpropagation and compensating in gradients to avoid numerical underflow in low-precision training.
example: Stabilize float16 gradient computation.
caveat: Scaling must be reversed before applying the optimizer update.

definition: Reduced use of information placed in middle context positions in some long-context tasks.
example: Test evidence placed at different document positions.
caveat: The effect varies by model, task, and prompt.

definition: Running model inference with reduced-precision representations or arithmetic.
example: Deploy a quantized model on a memory-limited device.
caveat: Bit width alone is insufficient to predict quality or latency.

definition: Learning low-rank weight updates while keeping original base weights frozen.
example: Adapt a model with two small update matrices per target layer.
caveat: LoRA reduces trainable parameters, not automatically the base model's stored size.

definition: Approximating a matrix with one having a smaller rank.
example: Compress a weight matrix.
caveat: Approximation can remove important low-energy directions.

definition: A gated recurrent architecture with a cell state designed to retain and update information over time.
example: Model long sequential dependencies.
caveat: It mitigates but does not eliminate long-context difficulties.

definition: Methods that use data or experience to fit models rather than specifying every decision rule by hand.
example: Learn to predict delivery delays from past orders.
caveat: Not every automated program is machine learning.

definition: Averaging per-class metrics with equal class weight.
example: Report macro F1 on imbalanced categories.
caveat: Small classes can have high influence and high uncertainty.

definition: Selecting the answer receiving the most votes across candidates or models.
example: Aggregate several model predictions.
caveat: A majority can still be systematically wrong.

definition: A neural sequence-model family using selective state-space computations.
example: Model text with a recurrent-state alternative to attention.
caveat: The family includes variants; properties depend on the specific architecture.

definition: Methods seeking lower-dimensional structure underlying high-dimensional observations.
example: Recover a curved low-dimensional representation.
caveat: The manifold assumption may not hold for all data.

definition: A measure of separation between a decision boundary and training points.
example: Maximize separation in a linear SVM.
caveat: Definitions and normalization differ across models.

definition: A probability obtained by summing or integrating over other variables.
example: Compute class prevalence from a joint distribution.
caveat: Marginal and conditional probabilities can differ greatly.

definition: A stochastic process whose next state depends on the current state rather than the full past.
example: Build a sampler with local state transitions.
caveat: The state must contain enough relevant information.

definition: Sampling methods that construct a Markov chain with a desired stationary distribution.
example: Approximate a Bayesian posterior.
caveat: Finite chains can mix poorly or fail to converge adequately.

definition: A decision model with states, actions, transitions, rewards, and a Markov assumption.
example: Formalize sequential control.
caveat: Real-world tasks may only be approximated by the chosen MDP.
